summary.text: 见 means “see” or “observe.” It is the standardized simplified form of 見, whose eye and human figure together depict seeing. The lower figure is identified differently in accounts of ancient and received forms.

formation.text: The traditional graph 見 is pictographic: an eye above a human figure depicts seeing. Ancient forms are analyzed with 卩, a kneeling person; the received form is parsed as 目 and 儿. 见 is the standardized simplified form of 見, though its particular path from cursive writing is not established here.

components.text: In 見, 目 is the prominent eye and part of the depiction of seeing. Both the ancient-form and received-form analyses identify this eye element.

In the ancient-form analysis of 見, 卩 is a kneeling person beneath the eye, completing the person-and-eye depiction. The received-form analysis instead identifies the lower figure as 儿; these are stage-specific analyses, not evidence of corruption.
In the received-form analysis of 見, 儿 is the human figure paired with 目 in the depiction of seeing. This differs from the ancient-form analysis, which identifies the lower figure as 卩.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms of 見 are indexed and described as a prominent eye above a human figure. A received-form analysis parses 見 as 儿 plus 目. The evidence does not provide a dated sequence of intermediate graphic changes.
The simplified-character standard maps 見 to 见. A cursive origin for 见 is proposed, but a specific exemplar and detailed transition are not established.

uncertainties.text: The reported oracle-bone and bronze uses include seeing, audience, and other grammatical or lexical uses, but their chronology and a complete sequence of meaning changes are unresolved.

One oracle-bone use is reported as 見 read 獻, “offer sacrificial goods.” This may reflect reuse of the graph to write a similar-sounding word rather than a change in the meaning “see”; the inscription examples and independent sound comparison are unavailable. This does not establish the pronunciation of the depicted person or object.
A proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison appears in the record, but the evidence cited here does not support it, so no language-family etymology is asserted.

senses.text: Seeing is the core meaning assigned in the received dictionary account and reported for oracle-bone and bronze uses; no specific earliest inscription date is established.
Audience is reported among oracle-bone and bronze uses. Its date and chronological relation to “see” are unresolved.
A passive auxiliary use is reported for bronze inscriptions. Its date and development from the seeing sense are unresolved.

senses.gloss: offer sacrificial goods, written with 見 and read 獻
senses.text: One oracle-bone use is reported as 見 read 獻, “offer sacrificial goods.” The proposed explanation is borrowing the graph for a similar-sounding word, not a demonstrated semantic extension; the inscription evidence and sound comparison are unavailable.
The current simplified character is glossed with meanings including seeing, observing, and perceiving.

limitations.text: The reported historical uses lack a specimen-level date sequence that would connect audience, passive, and offering uses to one another or to the seeing sense.
